result:
I've built PERF-1b-i: the new interactions spec, its budget file, the three PERF-1a hygiene fixes and doc 168. All the self-checks the task asks for passed. One part differs from the task text and needs B's ruling.

**Needs B ruling: how the range drag is shown to be live.** The task says to watch `[data-range-end]`, but the app never renders it for a range dragged on a clip body. It only appears for an all-tracks range (`ArrangementLane.tsx` l.1016–1026). The spec reads the end time from the range label inside the clip instead (e.g. `00:07.525 – 00:10.525 · 3.000 s`) and requires it to grow during the drag. This is written at the top of `a-round-214.md` and in doc 168; I did not treat it as a STOP. A smaller change: a clip click is shown by the Clip Gain fader becoming enabled, because the fader is always on screen and counting it proves nothing.

**What changed (5 granted files edited, 3 new files):**
- **New spec** `perf/studio-lab-interactions.perf.spec.ts`, with its own budget file `perf/budgets.interactions.json` (144 rows). It measures clip click, zoom with 1 and 30 clips, the four drags stopped and playing, and play/pause.
- **Reset after each drag:** Ctrl+Z is pressed only if the Undo button's title changed, so a drag that did nothing cannot undo the Add. A range is cleared with a click on the clip body, because Escape does not clear it. Every reset is then checked.
- **PERF-1a fixes:**
  - S3: the run fails if no React renderer was injected or its major version is not 18; both reports now have a `reactRenderer` field.
  - S6: `harness.audio-running` now also needs at least one `start()` call.
  - S4: the fixed 2 s wait is replaced by waiting for the clips and waveforms.
- **Docs:** doc 163 (l.67 plus one pointer sentence on l.152), doc 167 (post-PASS lines) and the new doc 168, whose status is left as "C round 214 check pending".

**Checks run on the final tree:**
- `npm run typecheck`: exit 0.
- `npm run lint`: exit 0. Its 205 warnings were already in `app/`, which this round did not touch.
- Biome: `npx biome check perf/` checks nothing because `biome.json` only covers `app/`. A scratch copy with `perf/` included came back clean.
- New spec, run twice: exit 0 both times, 314 s and 299 s against the 12 min limit, no failures. Every count row gave identical samples in both runs.
- PERF-1a, once: exit 0. All 316 rows were measured 3 times, all asserts passed, and all 167 deterministic medians equal `a-round-212/perf-run-1.json`.
- Mutants M1–M4, on a `/tmp` copy: each failed on its named row. M4 failed on that row only.
- Frozen file list: rc 0 at the start and at the end.
- Code-reviewer: 8/10, no Critical or High. I fixed its M1 and five Low findings. M2 is noted as a limit: the ±2 tolerance cannot catch drift in small ratio rows, which PERF-1a shares.

**What the numbers say (doc 168 §"PERF candidates"):**
- **Range, fade-in, trim and move:** each re-renders the whole provider on every mouse move (96–101 components per move), so each should get the fader treatment.
- **Fade, trim and move also restart clips on release:** one clip with 1 clip, all 30 with 30 clips (measured for fade; for trim and move it is inferred from the shared commit path).
- **Zoom key, clip click, play/pause:** OK. Zoom costs 95 components per key with 1 clip and 240 with 30.

These are proposals for B to rule on at round 216.

**Known gaps:**
- Trim and move release restarts with 30 clips were not measured.
- The new spec fails on uncaught page errors; PERF-1a only counts them. My runs had none.
- `npm run test:perf` with both specs together was run only in the scratch mutant run, not on the clean tree.

The reviewer's architecture note proposes moving the helpers the two specs share into `perf/lib/` (the existing PERF-HARNESS-SHARED-LIB signal). It is copied verbatim in the report for B and root; I did not do it.

Report: `tmp/studio-real-loop/a-round-214.md`; evidence is in `tmp/studio-real-loop/a-round-214/`. I did not commit or push, and I did not mark the backlog complete.
